newsitem.title: JAPAN: Overseas 16MB DRAM spot prices on the rise - paper.
newsitem.headline: Overseas 16MB DRAM spot prices on the rise - paper.

text.p: Overseas spot prices of the most widely used 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips are sharply recovering and they have reached $12 to $15 per unit, almost double the price at the beginning of September, a Japanese newspaper said on Friday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun economic daily said that the price rises are due to inventory adjustments at personal computer makers and smaller shipments by chip makers.
Chipmakers are currently conducting price negotiations with large-volume customers for their October chip shipments and the rising spot prices are encouraging them, the paper said.
